To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
226Ra excess over its parent 230Th is observed in mid-ocean ridge basalt (MORB), and that the 226Ra/230Th ratio in MORB is higher than the ratio in mantle source.

226Ra excess over its parent 230Th in mid-ocean ridge basalt samples from the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, East Pacific Rise, and South Atlantic Ridge are observed, and that the excesses constrain the time scale of magma transport from melting in the mantle to eruption to less than 1,000 years.
the 226Ra/230Th ratios in MORBs from the East Pacific Rise (EPR) are significantly elevated relative to the secular equilibrium value of 0.002.

the study of the geochemical and geophysical processes that control the formation of oceanic island basaltic magmas and their subsequent transfer to the surface.

the study of the chemical composition of the earth’s crust and the earth’s mantle, the study of the processes which have formed the crust and the mantle and the study of the geochemical and geophysical evolution of the earth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
226Ra excess in MORB is the result of the kinetic effect, which occurs in the melting process in the mantle.
the 226Ra/230Th ratio in MORB is a function of time since separation of melt from the mantle, and that the time scale is of the order of 1000 years.
the timescale of the entire process from melting to eruption is less than a thousand years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the timescale of mantle melting and magma transport is on the order of 10(5) years.
the 226Ra/228Ra ratios of the MORB samples are consistent with a mantle source with a Th/U ratio of ~0.1 and a 226Ra/238U ratio of 0.1.
226Ra is a very useful tool in studying mantle melting and magma transfer processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 226Ra/230Th and 226Ra/228Th ratios of mid-ocean- ridge basalts (MORBs) are not in equilibrium, and that these ratios provide a new and powerful constraint on the time scale of mantle melting.
the 226Ra–226Ra disequilibria are produced in the mantle and are not due to the contamination by young sediments.
the 226Ra and its daughter 210Pb can be used as a powerful new tracer of magmatic processes.
